tagline: Tasks that can pay you — or fine you — when you finish them.
description:
Tasks handles three kinds of work: persistent tasks that are always there, one-time tasks with a due date, and periodic tasks that come back daily, weekly or monthly. Each one can carry a description and belong to several categories at once.

What makes it different is what happens on completion. A task can be worth an amount — positive as a reward, negative as a penalty — and that amount is written straight into a category in Budget. Tasks can also be timed: start the clock, pause it, and the reward is calculated from an hourly rate and the time you actually tracked.

Everything is kept in a history of completions, and the same list is reachable from a public web page for your Apps Hub account.
capabilities: Persistent, one-time and periodic tasks, with daily, weekly or monthly recurrence.
Due date and time, with overdue tasks marked.
One-shot completion, or a timer with start, pause, continue and stop.
Reward or penalty per completion — a fixed amount, or an hourly rate applied to the time tracked.
Discard tracked time when it should not count.
Public web page for your Apps Hub account.

integrations.name: Budget
integrations.summary: Pick a Budget category on a task and give it an amount. Completing the task pays that amount into the category — or takes it out, if the amount is negative. Timed tasks pay the hourly rate for the time actually tracked. Without Budget, the task still works; there is simply no reward.
integrations.requires: Budget installed, and its App API enabled in Apps Hub → Settings → App APIs. The switch is off by default.
